title: Graceful SSE resume and partial-output handling for Hosted API disconnects
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Multiple enterprise customers reported truncated/partial responses and abrupt SSE connections when using the hosted /v1/streams endpoints behind customer proxies and internal gateways. Symptoms observed: final tokens missing, last-event-id gaps, client-side reconnects that produce duplicate or inconsistent completions, and tokens not flushed to logs. This ticket defines the reproducible conditions, root cause hypotheses, chosen remediation, and rollout plan for a hosted-side fix that (1) makes SSE output atomic at event boundaries, (2) provides a resume token/last-event-id semantic for safe reconnects, and (3) introduces conservative server-side buffering/keepalive to avoid mid-stream truncation on common proxies. The goal is to reduce customer-facing truncation incidents by 95% and provide deterministic behavior for clients that retry after transient network failures.
reproduction_steps:
1) Use curl to open an SSE stream to the hosted endpoint with a long-running generation (500+ tokens) and small chunk_size to force many events.
2) Introduce a TCP reset or simulate proxy idle timeout after ~3s of inactivity (Cloudflare/NGINX).
3) Observe that client receives an 'event: done' may be missing and last event payload ends mid-token.
4) Use Last-Event-ID header on reconnect and attempt to resume; currently server rejects or replays from start, causing duplicates or inconsistent final state.
Example curl: curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=open-rl.mini"
root_cause_analysis:
1) Our streaming runtime flush path sometimes emits partial frames when a write syscall encounters an EPIPE or early connection close; the output buffer is not checkpointed into a durable resume state.
2) We lacked a lightweight resume token per 'SSE chunk' boundary (not per-token) which means there is no safe, idempotent replay point.
3) Network intermediaries (proxies/gateways) that close idle TCP after a short window drop connections while backend is computing longer prefix tokens; our keepalive interval is too coarse for some environments.
4) Dedicated and Private deployments showed fewer reports because local networking often preserves connections; hosted customers behind corporate proxies are the main affected group.
5) Log/telemetry gaps: some token-level emission events are never flushed to persistent logs when the connection closes during syscall failures, making postmortem reconstruction hard.
proposed_fix:
High-level approach in three coordinated changes: 
A) Emission atomicity: change server-side SSE encoder to only emit events at token-boundary-safe frames. Introduce a small per-event buffer and ensure we mark the event boundary in an append-only resume log.
B) Resume token: attach a concise resume_id to each SSE event (base64 of stream_id + offset + crc8) and support Last-Event-ID on the endpoint to resume from resume_id. Resume semantics: replay from the last durable token boundary and mark the previous partial event as truncated if it didn't reach durability. 
C) Keepalive/flow: tighten server-side keepalive and introduce optional sub-second ping events for customers annotated as behind proxies. Expose new header X-Redwood-Resume-Support: true/false in handshake.
D) Fallback: when resume not available (older client), provide deterministic fallback: either deliver a final non-streaming consolidated completion or return explicit error code instructing client to retry non-streaming.
E) Telemetry: emit resume_id, final_status (complete|truncated|failed) and last_flushed_offset to logs/metrics for SLA tracking.
implementation_details:
- Code changes: streaming runtime (golang) encoder + resume log writer; API gateway handler for Last-Event-ID parsing; runtime-safe resume recovery path to replay from durable offset.
- Resume token format: v1:{stream_id}:{flush_offset}:{crc8} base64-encoded to keep headers compact.
- Backward compatibility: if client does not send Last-Event-ID, server behaves as today but with better atomic flush to reduce truncation.
- Edge cases: function-calling streams will include resume markers but must ensure side-effect idempotency (see dependency ENG-4811). We will surface a new function-calling flag in the protocol to disallow resume when server-side actions already executed and not idempotent.
- Testing: unit tests for resume token encoding/decoding, integration tests simulating connection resets, and long-tail soak tests behind Envoy/NGINX proxies with varying idle timeouts.
deploy_plan:
1) Canary rollout to 5% of hosted traffic for read-only clients (non-enterprise) with metric hooks.
2) Second canary: enable resume handshake header for 10 targeted enterprise customers who reported incidents, collect logs for two days.
3) Gradual ramp to 50% then 100% if metrics pass.
4) Release will be labeled runtime-2.3.1-hotfix and coordinated with Customer Success for targeted customers.
5) For Dedicated/Private we will publish a backport suggestion (configuration toggles) and a migration note for on-prem kernel versions.
rollback_plan:
If we observe increase in duplicate outputs or a new class of truncation: revert to previous runtime image and toggle X-Redwood-Resume-Support off via config. Maintain emergency runbook to offer non-streaming export to affected customers while rollback completes.
Hotfix rollback latency target: <30 minutes for critical regressions.
qa_plan:
- Unit tests for resume token correctness and crc mismatch.
- Integration: simulated proxy timeouts (Envoy with connection close at 5s, 10s), assert that clients either resume correctly or receive final consolidated completion.
- Chaos tests: random TCP RST injected at server output path during long-generation.
- Customer verification: coordinate with 3 customers to validate resume behavior in their environments.
- Automated e2e in staging with realistic token counts (100-1000 tokens) and both streaming and function-calling payloads.
monitoring_and_alerts:
New metrics to add: stream_resume_attempts, stream_resume_success_rate, stream_truncated_rate, last_flushed_offset_histogram, sse_keepalive_pings_sent.
Alerting: page on stream_truncated_rate > 0.5% for 10 minutes for enterprise-tier tenants.
Dashboards: per-tenant timeline of resume_id reuse and per-region truncation heatmap.
Logs: include resume_id and final_status in structured logs; add a debug mode to capture token diffs for truncated streams.
